test_title: PYST 53: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 08 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Globalization has increased cross-border flows of technology. What policy under globalization encourages technology transfer?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Automatic route for FDI**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Automatic route for FDI (Foreign Direct Investment)** allows foreign investors to invest in Indian businesses without requiring prior approval from the government or the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
• This policy ensures a smoother and faster inflow of foreign capital, including technology transfer, into the Indian economy.
 
• Under globalization, the automatic route has been instrumental in enabling sectors like IT, manufacturing, and renewable energy to gain access to advanced technologies from foreign entities.
 
• It encourages multinational corporations to establish joint ventures or wholly-owned subsidiaries in India, thereby facilitating technological advancements and innovation.
 
• As per the **FDI Policy 2023**, 100% FDI is allowed under the automatic route in various sectors like automobiles, computer software, and hardware, promoting cross-border technology exchange.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nationalisation**

 
 
• It refers to the process where the government takes ownership and control of private sector businesses or industries.
 
• Nationalization usually occurs to protect strategic industries or ensure equal access to resources and services.
 
 
 
• **Import substitution policy**
 
 
• This policy focuses on reducing dependency on imported goods by promoting domestic production.
 
• While it aims to strengthen local industries, it may hinder globalization by discouraging foreign investments and technology transfer.
 
• It was widely adopted in India during the pre-liberalization era (before 1991).
 
 
 
• **Licensing raj**
 
 
• The licensing raj refers to India's pre-1991 economic system, which required businesses to obtain licenses and permits to operate in various sectors.
 
• This bureaucratic system restricted foreign investments and technology transfer by creating regulatory hurdles.
 
• It was dismantled after the 1991 economic reforms, paving the way for liberalization and globalization.
